Season 3 of “ Nobody Wants This ” reached 6.2 million views in its first four days of streaming on Netflix .
Compared to previous seasons of the Adam Brody and Kristen Bell-led comedy series, that’s a decrease: Season 1 debuted with 10.3 million views in 2024 and Season 2 debuted 8.6 million views in 2025. Ranked against other recent titles, however, the project isn’t doing badly: This ranks as the biggest opening weekend for a returning comedy series on Netflix in all of 2026. It should also be noted that when Season 2 was released, catch-up viewing was strong, with Season 1 returning to the chart for two more weeks. This time around, viewership of Seasons 1 and 2 did jump by 200% compared to the week before Season 3 was released, but not enough for either season to return to the Top 10.
“Nobody Wants This” Season 3 was the second-most-watched TV title of the week of Oct. 19-25 on Netflix’s weekly rankings, following Josh Hartnett’s “Below,” which hit 7.7 million views in its third week on the chart. And the top title overall on Netflix that week was on the movies chart: Ben Affleck’s “Animals” hit 10.7 million views, also in its third week. And on the non-English-language TV chart, Part 4 of “Lupin” led the pack with 6.4 million views and brought renewed attention to Part 1, which took 10th place with 2.1 million views.
Back on the English-language TV chart, the No. 3 spot went to “The Diplomat” Season 4 with 5.5 million views in its second chart week, up from No. 5 with 4.8 million views the week before. The Mike Tyson docuseries “Tyson” landed at No. 4 for the second week in a row with 3.8 million views, followed by “Love Is Blind” Season 11 with 3.7 million views in its second week.
“East of Eden” had its fourth week on the chart at No. 6 with 3.6 million views, followed by the debut of “The New Stanford Prison Experiment” with 2.6 million views in five days.
